desc: nemesis attacks the repo's own dev environment only. A hard gate is checked at every cycle start, before any active testing: an owner-signed, non-expired authorization.yml with an explicit attestation; every target on the allowlist and passing the host floor on its resolved address (loopback, or a private address the owner-signed file names and marks dev; any public address refused), with every production domain on scope.forbidden; dev environments only; and no .nemesis/STOP file. Any failure means file a BLOCKED issue and stop. Separately, a kill switch halts a running cycle (authorization invalid or expired, a target resolving off-allowlist or to a public or unknown address, a prohibited action needed, an anomaly or error-rate spike, a single-packet batch behaving unexpectedly, or a STOP file) and files a HALT issue. The methodology runs Pass 0 residue intake, Pass 1 recon and multi-tier surface, Pass 2 auth/session/step-up, Pass 3 authorization (highest value), Pass 4 injection, Pass 5 business logic (where the money is), Pass 6 API/config hygiene, Pass 7 detection-integrity, then triage and filing. Six bypass classes A to F run every domain every cycle, for outsider and insider alike. It files security-labelled GitHub issues naming the file and seam, keeps state under .nemesis/, and hands findings to /forge, which puts almost all in its red tier. Fix-mode is off by default.
title: /nemesis — authorized red-team, dev only
